results:
The search results support the PPP's role as a major opposition force, though most of the evidence is from 2013 and 2022, not the present.

- **2013 election:** Dawn's party history says the PPP became the largest opposition party in the National Assembly that year, while holding a majority in Sindh and forming the provincial government there. The party became the largest opposition party in the National Assembly. However, in Sindh it secured a majority and formed a government.
- **2018–2022 period:** A Carnegie analysis describes the PPP as a conventional opposition party that has resisted the PTI federal government mainly from its Sindh base, the party has resisted the interventions of the PTI central government (locally perceived to be belligerent) and played a leading role in oppositional politics in Pakistan. A June 2022 article by Asma Faiz notes that with 56 seats in the current National Assembly, the PPP played a pivotal role in the opposition to the PTI government.
- **Caveat:** Some results describe the PPP as the largest opposition bloc in 2013 based on pre-election projections, so they are not official outcomes. The results also don't cover the party's position after 2022, so for its current standing you'd need a more recent search.

content.title: PPP returns to the Centre stage

results:
I didn't find the Wikipedia article itself, but several sources cover the PPP's opposition periods.

- **1990:** After the IJI won and Nawaz Sharif became prime minister, Benazir Bhutto took up the opposition leader role. Benazir's government had been removed by President Ghulam Ishaq Khan over corruption charges, and the IJI then won the election. Benazir became opposition leader.
- **1997:** The PML-N won 137 National Assembly seats, and the PPP finished second with 18 seats. PML-N came to power with 137 seats in the National Assembly and PPP came second with 18 seats.
- **2002:** The PPP came second with 81 seats, behind PML-Q, which formed the government. Pakistan Muslim League - Quaid (PML-Q) formed the government after securing 126 seats in the 2002 election. The PPP came second with 81 seats.
- **2013:** The PPP became the largest opposition party in the National Assembly, even though it won a majority and formed the government in Sindh. The party became the largest opposition party in the National Assembly. However, in Sindh it secured a majority and formed a government. Syed Khurshid Shah served as opposition leader from 2013 to 2018. He served as the Opposition Leader of the National Assembly from 2013 to 2018 until the incumbent government put in place the caretaker set-up.
- **2018:** The sources I found don't name the PPP's leader in this period. One says the opposition took a high of 150 to 165 seats in the 15th National Assembly (2018–2022). A Carnegie piece on the PPP's role in opposition says the party commenced a "long march" from Karachi to Islamabad in February 2022 to try to oust the PTI government. The Wikipedia snippet notes the party's current standing as the largest in the Senate and second-largest party in the National Assembly.

The 1990, 1997, and 2013 details are well supported. For 2018, the sources only establish that the PPP was in opposition to the PTI government, and they don't confirm who held the opposition leader post. The 2002 entry is a second-place finish, and the sources don't show it was an opposition leader role.

content.text:
**Short answer: 3 times, in 1990, 1997 and 2013.** This is my reading of the sources. None of them states the count directly.

- **1990:** The IJI won and Nawaz Sharif became prime minister. Benazir Bhutto then led the opposition.
- **1997:** The PML-N won 137 seats and the PPP came second with 18.
- **2013:** The PPP became the largest opposition party in the National Assembly, and Khurshid Shah was opposition leader from 2013 to 2018.

I left out two cases:
- **2002:** The PPP came second, but the sources don't show it held the main opposition role. From memory, the MMA's Maulana Fazlur Rehman became opposition leader, though that part is not from the sources.
- **2018:** The PPP opposed the PTI government but was not the lead opposition party. From memory, the PML-N's Shehbaz Sharif was opposition leader, though that part is not from the sources.

Sources:
- [Dawn – Pakistan Peoples Party](https://www.dawn.com/news/1404648)
- [Carnegie – The peculiar case of the PPP as an opposition party](https://carnegieendowment.org/research/2022/03/the-peculiar-case-of-the-pakistan-peoples-party-as-an-opposition-party)
- [ARY News – Syed Khurshid Shah](https://arynews.tv/syed-khurshid-shah)
- [The News – PPP returns to the Centre stage](https://www.thenews.pk/tns/detail/963114-ppp-returns-to-the-centre-stage)
